reply_text:
I found four issues worth fixing before merge:

1. **[P1] Short previews lose text and always get an ellipsis** — `src/excerpt.js:6–8`  
   There’s no check for text already within the limit. `excerpt('hello world', 20)` returns `"hello…"` instead of `"hello world"`; empty input returns `"…"`. This contradicts the README’s unchanged-short-text and ellipsis-only-on-removal guarantees. Return early when the input fits.

2. **[P2] The helpers aren’t connected to card rendering** — `src/card.js:1–2`  
   `card()` still returns `entry.body.trim()`; neither `toPlain()` nor `excerpt()` is called anywhere outside tests. As written, merging this branch won’t change the preview under a card: long Markdown bodies still appear unchanged. Wire the helpers into the card path and add an integration test.

3. **[P2] A word ending exactly at the limit is unnecessarily dropped** — `src/words.js:2–4`  
   `slice(0, limit)` excludes the space *at* `limit`. Consequently, `excerpt('hello world again', 11)` produces `"hello…"` rather than `"hello world…"`, even though both words fit. Include the boundary position when looking for a separating space. The existing test at limit `7` currently codifies this off-by-one behavior.

4. **[P2] Markdown stripping deletes literal content** — `src/plain.js:3`  
   Removing every underscore, asterisk, tilde, and backtick treats literal characters as formatting. For example, `toPlain('Use foo_bar')` returns `"Use foobar"`, changing an identifier in the preview. Strip actual Markdown syntax rather than those characters globally, and cover literal punctuation in tests.

**Validation:** All four existing tests pass, but they miss these cases. Reviewed `main...excerpt-helper` at `59856d7`; no files changed.
